q: A customer sent me a CDP supply chain request. Do I have to respond, and what does it cost?
title: CDP supply chain request: respond or not?
short: No law makes you respond to a CDP supply chain request, but your customer will see whether you did, and many buyers use it in supplier reviews. If only customers requested you, CDP generally charges you no admin fee. The fee applies if an investor group also requested you or you disclose on your own.

sections.h: Who is asking, and what they see
p: A CDP request reaches a company in one of four ways, and the CDP Portal lists which ones apply to you:
ul: A customer that is a CDP Supply Chain member. This is the supply chain request; you get a direct link.
Investors that sign CDP's Letter to the Board, its Capital Markets Signatories. You also get a direct link.
An initiative your company is part of.

p: A Supply Chain member pays CDP to send questionnaires to its suppliers and to see their answers in one place. Your customer sees whether you responded and, if you did, your answers and score. A missing response shows as a non-response, which usually leads to a follow-up from their procurement or sustainability team.

sections.h: How to decide whether to respond
ul: Respond if the customer is a large share of your revenue, if the request comes with a supplier code or contract clause on climate data, or if they have said non-response affects supplier ratings.
Ask first if you are unsure: ask whether a short emissions summary by email would do for this cycle, and from when they expect a full CDP response.
Decline only after telling the customer why and what you can send instead. Silence is the worst option.

sections.h: When CDP charges a fee, and when it does not
p: CDP's admin fee is generally waived if you were requested only by Supply Chain members (your customers), Banks Program members, Private Markets members or the RE100 initiative. A supplier asked only by its customers usually discloses without paying CDP.

The fee applies if CDP's Capital Markets signatories, its investor group, also requested you, or if you choose to disclose without being asked. It is the same for the SME and full questionnaires, it is not refundable, and companies headquartered in India can choose CDP's lower Essential tier, aimed at SMEs.

The CDP Portal shows who requested you. If you are exempt, the Submission Lead sees a single option labelled 'No fee payable' on the 'Choose admin fee' page and must still select it, or the questionnaire cannot be submitted. Ask CDP's Help Center if you are unsure whether a fee applies.

Since 2024 CDP uses one integrated corporate questionnaire, covering climate, forests, water and other themes, and a shorter SME questionnaire. Revenue and employee numbers decide which one you are eligible for. The SME version asks for the basics: your emissions method, Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions, energy use, and targets and reduction actions if you have them.
Confirm with your customer which version they expect. If they accept the SME version, it is usually the right start for an MSME.

sections.h: What to prepare before you open the portal
ol: Pick the reporting year, usually your financial year April to March, and the organisational boundary (which plants and offices).
Calculate Scope 1 from fuel purchases and Scope 2 from electricity bills, with the emission factors and their sources.
Note any Scope 3 categories you can estimate, or say plainly that you have not yet calculated them.
Write a short description of reduction actions with dates and numbers, such as a solar install or a boiler fuel switch.
Decide with your management whether the response is public or shared only with requesting customers.

senseible: Senseible calculates Scope 1 and 2 from your invoices and electricity bills, with the factor and source document behind each line. Its team can draft the response from your verified records and policies, you review and submit it, and it cannot promise a score or act as a third-party verifier.
